title: C3065 — Front safety belt anchor and pretensioner LH
introduction:
This reference identifies the left-hand front safety-belt anchor and pretensioner connector. I read it like an address book: the housing drawing identifies the connector, the cavity labels lead into the circuit table, and the service-parts table keeps the catalog identities together. The function descriptions tie this connection to the front driver-side pretensioner.

Use the drawing and tables together to understand those identities. The physical viewing side, gauge convention and meanings of the Size and Used codes are unspecified. This is an identification guide; physical access, probing, testing and replacement require the applicable service instructions.

items.name: Qualified service and preparation
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Any hands-on work requires the selected job’s depowering, handling, specified test equipment and restoration instructions. Consult the [SRS overview](#/document/G1696290) and [pyrotechnic-device precautions](#/document/G1693191) before service.

items.name: Connections and fault diagnosis
items.detail: Connector-position-assurance tabs and shorting bars affect electrical configuration. A plug can look attached while an assurance tab remains improperly seated, producing a fault. Use the exact connection and verification instructions. For diagnosis, record the fault information and use the restraint-specific diagnostic path; do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test.

edits.why: I use the circular face, its surrounding housing and the broad extension to the left as landmarks within this drawing. Read the printed cavity labels against the assignment table below; their positions connect the illustration to the circuit descriptions.

Start with Cavity, then read across the same row for circuit identity, color, gauge and function. The function descriptions distinguish the driver-side pretensioner’s positive and negative connections. Those signs describe the circuit assignments; they are not instructions to apply power. The terminal column carries a preassembly designation rather than an individual terminal service number.

The pigtail entries share a shell identification but retain distinct service-part identities; this reference gives no selection rule between them. Keep the harness gauge and each pigtail gauge attached to their respective table entries, without treating either as a replacement-wire recommendation. Number identifies the catalog entry, Service Part identifies the service item, Engineering Shell cross-references the housing, and Image names a catalog image file.
